News Items 
 
Kildare TY Students Invited to Join Ireland’s Leading Enterprise Challenge 
Kildare County Council’s Local Enterprise Office announced the opening of 
registration for the Kildare Student Enterprise Programme for the academic year 
2025/26 (see page 9). 
 
Library Services - Skills for Life 
Skills for Life is a new national programme in public libraries across Ireland. It offers 
practical learning to help with everyday life—like using the internet, managing 
money, understanding media, finding work, staying healthy, and living sustainably 
(see page 12). 
 
Risk Management 
A review of the Corporate Risk Register took place in June 2025. The Head of 
Internal Audit, Risk and Governance is working with the Council Departments to 
complete and document the actions from the review. The next review is scheduled 
for September 2025 (see page 20). 
 
Brigid, Spirit of Kildare Programme 
Planning has commenced for the Brigid, Spirit of Kildare festival 2026. This festival is 
set to take place across the county over the February bank holiday weekend and will 
build on the success of last year’s festival under the theme ‘Her Spirit, Our Story’ 
(see page 49). 
 
Community Climate Action Program Fund 
Twenty-four projects from the county were approved by the Department of 
Environment, Climate and Communications (DECC) for the Community Climate 
Action Fund grant. Grantees have 18 months to complete the projects (see page 56).

Road Safety - Speed Limit Review 
Briefings were held with elected members in advance of the public consultation 
process for the proposed 30 km/hr speed limits in housing estates that are taken in 
charge across the county (see page 63). 
 
Outdoor Recreational Plan  
The preparation of an action plan for outdoor recreation is underway. It is planned to 
have draft plan completed by the end of October (see page 69).  
 
Planning Control – Online Map 
The Planning Control Section has launched an online map integrated with the 
Enforcement System and GIS mapping. This will display locations of unauthorised 
development sites and related points. The system is scheduled to go live on 
Monday, 8 September 2025 (see page 74). 
 
Kildare Failte – Taste of Kildare 
Taste of Kildare returned to Naas Racecourse for a second consecutive year on 16 
and 17 August, showcasing Kildare as a premier food destination (see pages 78/79). 
 
Erasmus+ Repower Regions   
Kildare County Council, in collaboration with eleven European partners, continues to 
progress the Erasmus+ Repower Regions project, which supports regional 
cooperation and skills development in the heating and cooling sector.   
The project is progressing according to timelines (see page 83).

Diary/Calendar 
 
Kildare County Council Shortlisted in Four Categories at the Irish Planning 
Institute’s Planning Awards 2025 
The Council has been shortlisted in four categories at the Irish Planning Institute's 
Planning Awards 2025. This recognition highlights the Council’s commitment to 
excellence in planning and sustainable development.  The national winners of this 
prestigious competition will be revealed at a gala ceremony in Clontarf Castle Hotel 
on Thursday 25 September 2025 (see page 8). 
 
Register of Electors - Presidential Election – 24 October 2025 
In advance of the forthcoming Presidential Election, the following important dates for 
registration apply:  
Postal Vote Applications: Deadline for submission is 29 September 2025 
Ordinary Vote Applications: Deadline for submission is 07 October 2025 (see page 
10). 
 
Kildare County Archives and Local Studies 
The annual John Devoy Commemoration takes place in Naas Library and Cultural 
Centre on 25 September at 7.00pm (see page 13). 
 
Health and Safety Conference 2025 
The 2025 Health and Safety Conference will take place on Tuesday, 21 October 
(see page 17). 
 
Budget 2026 
Budget 2026 briefing meeting is to be held on-line on Monday, 10 November 2025. 
The Statutory Budget meeting will be held on Monday, 17 November 2025 (see page 
20).

Emily Square, Athy – Public Realm Official Opening 
Minister Martin Heydon will officially open Emily Square on Friday, 12 September at 
a public event taking place in the Square (see page 21). 
 
Staff Energy Awareness  
A Staff Energy Awareness Day will take place on 29 October during Climate Action 
Week from 9.30am to 3.00pm with experts attending from across the industry 
focusing on improving Home Energy (see page 54). 
 
Climate Week 
The Climate Action Office is preparing to hold Climate Week during the last week of 
October. Given the time of year, we hope to have items that embrace the Halloween 
theme. Items will be inward facing while other items will be available to the public. 
This will expand the range and audience levels (see page 56). 
 
Local Community Development Committee  
The next meeting of the LCDC is scheduled for 16 October 2025 (see page 61). 
 
Local Enterprise Office – Women in Business 
Local Enterprise Office Kildare has announced the date for the annual National 
Women’s Enterprise Day to take place in Keadeen Hotel on 16 October (See page 
81) 
 
Local Enterprise Office - Focus on Tech  
Applications are open for the MERITS Tech Pre-Accelerator, where those with an 
idea or tech start-up are supported to validate their product/ service for market-fit. 
The programme will commence in late September and align with the upcoming Tech 
Cluster Meet-Up on 25 September (See page 82).

Heritage Week 
Kildare Library Service hosted 19 
events with an attendance of 658 
people. There was a wide range of 
workshops throughout the county to 
choose from, which included a 
Bodhrán workshop, Irish Lace 
Demonstration, Arts and crafts 
workshops, Genealogy Talk by 
James Durney, Lego brick artist with 
Jessica Farrell, ‘Seal le Ré Ó 
Laighléis’ with author Ré Ó Laighléis, 
Making Spinning Wheels and many 
more events.  
 
Summer Stars 2025 
 
A total of 4,266 children from County 
Kildare took part in Summer Stars 
2025, the free national library 
programme encouraging children to 
read for fun during the school holidays. 
Whether it’s picture books, graphic 
novels, or audiobooks, every child 
could take part and enjoy reading at 
their own pace and were able to take 
part in a wide range of events 
including story times, author readings, 
games, concerts, arts and crafts and 
much more. 
By supporting children to embrace the 
joy of reading, libraries are helping 
them to develop skills for life - literacy 
skills, imagination and creativity, and 
to develop a lifelong love of reading.

Skills for Life 
Skills for Life is a new national 
programme in public libraries across 
Ireland. It offers practical learning to 
help with everyday life—like using the 
internet, managing money, 
understanding media, finding work, 
staying healthy, and living sustainably. 
It is available in all 30 local authority 
library services and covers six key 
areas: 
• 
Basic digital skills 
• 
Financial literacy 
• 
Media literacy 
• 
Business and employment skills 
• 
Health awareness 
• 
Sustainable living and 
environmental awareness 
 
Naas Library and Cultural Centre and 
Leixlip Community Library both hosted 
Bike Maintenance workshops as part 
of the programme in July. 
Healthy Ireland at Your Library 
The Irish Heart Foundation’s Mobile 
Health Unit and the Hidden Hearing 
Mobile Unit visited the Library in July.

Kildare County Archives and Local 
Studies 
The annual John Devoy 
Commemoration takes place in Naas 
Library and Cultural Centre on 25 
September at 7.00pm. Devoy’s chair, 
donated to Kildare County Council’s 
County Archives by Frank 
MacGabhann whose aunts, Alice 
Cumiskey (née Carragher) and Lily 
Carragher, looked after John Devoy in 
his final years in the U.S., will be on 
display at the event for the first time. It 
was transported to Ireland from the 
U.S.A., earlier this year with the 
assistance of the Department of 
Foreign Affairs, the Irish Consulate in 
New York and the Department of 
Culture, Communications and Sport.  
A short film by Donal Higgins, ‘John 
Devoy: the Greatest of the Fenians’, 
will also be shown. The Cathaoirleach 
will open the event. 
The Local Studies Librarian presented 
a talk ‘Tracing Your Family Tree - A 
Family Event’ in Naas Library and 
Cultural Centre on 15 July. 
During Heritage Week Local Studies 
was open to the public on 19 and 20 
August. Information on collections and 
a tour was given to those in 
attendance.

Creative Ireland Kildare 
Tóch | Dig – with Pamela De Brí, 
Shane Hynan and Sheena Malone.  
The launch of Tóch I Dig Phase II took 
place in Ballyteague GAA Hall on 
Saturday, 09 August. The launch of 
Phase II took the format of an informal 
feedback session on Phase I and an 
exploratory workshop on the future 
direction of the project. 
 
‘Tóch | Dig’ is a phased 
intergenerational community 
engagement project initiated by artists 
Pamela de Brí, Shane Hynan and 
Sheena Malone who are interested in 
working with communities of place and 
interest connected to bogs in north 
Kildare.  
 
Undercurrents: A Social and 
Ecological Story of Leixlip 
Leixlip-born artist Ian Nolan and 
sociologist Dr. Eamonn Slater leads 
tours of discovery, unearthing the 
undercurrents of Leixlip’s ongoing 
history and exploring the complex 
social and ecological worlds that make 
up the places we live. 
These free workshops took place in 
July. All events were livestreamed for 
accessibility 
Women+ Songwriting, Mentoring 
and Recording Camp 
Women+ Songwriting, Mentoring and 
Recording Camp was a free, week-
long creative programme for young 
female and gender-expansive 
songwriters (ages 12–15), designed to 
empower through mentorship, 
collaboration, and performance. 
Inspired by Gráinne Hunt and Megan 
O’Neill’s experiences as touring artists, 
the camp addressed the challenges 
WOMEN+ face in the music industry 
by offering support, representation, 
and community. Nine youth 
participants recorded a personal 
professional standard demo of their 
own song, written and produced with 
the assistance and accompaniment of 
music professionals, performing for an 
audience in the Riverbank Arts Centre 
in Newbridge. 
 
The Peatlands Immersive 
Experience - Monasterevin 
Launched at the Monasterevin 
Community Centre on 17 August and 
ran until 07 September, the Peatlands 
Immersive Installation is an exploration 
the ecological treasures that are the 
peatlands and wetlands of Ireland and

found within.  
 
The installation combines animated 
paintings, photography, field

Tina Claffey, Kathrine Geoghegan,

Municipal Art Collection Live on 
Kildare County Council (KCC)

Kildare Arts Service has collaborated 
with Kildare County Council’s IS 
Analyst Developer to publish the 
Municipal Art Collection onto KCC 
Power Apps. This new database has 
provided a better digitised system for 
the documentation, accessibility and 
auditing of artworks.  
 
 
Co-Creative Lab, Creative 
Collaborator’s Workshops and 
Walks 
The Co-Creative Lab, Creative 
Collaborator, Rachel Sweeney, has 
continued to deliver creative 
workshops and Deep Time Walks 
throughout August to community 
groups in Maynooth. These aim to 
creatively investigate Maynooth’s 
natural and man-made timelines, 
reflecting on how our carbon footprint 
impacts the world around us. The Co-
Creative Lab is a collaboration 
between Kildare County Council 
Climate Team, the Arts Service and 
Maynooth University. It is a recipient of 
the Creative Climate Action fund, an 
initiative from the Creative Ireland 
Programme.   
 
Kildare Dance Summer School 
Kildare Arts Service successfully 
delivered the bi-annual Kildare Dance 
Summer School on the grounds of St. 
Patrick’s College, Maynooth. This saw 
three days of inclusive dance and 
movement workshops that welcomed 
all abilities. Curated by Ailish Claffey, 
workshops were led by the Say 
Collective and facilitators from the 
amazing UK based Amici Dance

Farewell to Lucina Russell 
After almost 25 years with Kildare 
County Council, Lucina Russell 
stepped down as Arts Officer with 
Kildare Arts Service. Working 
alongside artists, arts communities, 
councillors and TDs, colleagues, Local 
Authority Arts Officers right across the 
country, local and national arts 
organisations, the Arts Council and 
Creative Ireland, Lucina worked 
tirelessly to support and resource 
quality arts and cultural experiences 
for the county and beyond. A new 
County Arts Officer post has now been 
advertised. 
 
Hawk Against the Dove Exhibition, 
Athy 
 
Hawk Against the Dove, a 
photographic exhibition confronting 
addiction in small-town Ireland was 
hosted at Art House, Athy in July and 
August. Curated by Anthony Haughey, 
it was a collaboration between 
Antoinette Foley and James Mahon. 
This exhibition offered an unflinching 
portrait of addiction, resilience and 
redemption in rural Ireland. Supported 
by Kildare Arts Service and Creative 
Places Athy. Antoinette’s journey from 
homelessness to a social housing 
tenancy under the Housing First 
Programme has been supported by 
the Homeless Team (Housing 
Department).  
 
Historic Athy Town Photograph  
Kildare County Council and Creative 
Places Athy recently celebrated and 
re-created an iconic photograph of 
Emily Square in Athy by photographer 
John Minihan. This was a collaboration 
with Artist in Residence Anthony 
Haughey at Art House, Athy and Athy 
Photography Society. Together, they 
invited the people of Athy to help 
recreate this iconic moment.

Housing 
Summary of Social Housing 
Assessments (SSHA) 2025 
Kildare County Council has 
commenced the Summary of Social 
Housing Assessment (SSHA) 2025.  
Only applicants approved with Kildare 
County Council as in need of social 
housing that have been previously 
requested to update their Housing file 
prior to 27 June 2025 will be required 
to complete this form.  Housing 
Assistance Payment (HAP) tenants, 
Rental Accommodation Scheme (RAS) 
tenants or transfer tenants are not 
required to complete this form.  The 
closing date for receipt of the SSHA 
forms is 12 September 2025.  Under 
the Departmental directive, failure to 
submit fully completed SSHA 2025 
form, along with relevant 
documentation, will result in the file 
being closed and the applicant being 
removed from the housing list.
